crime_highlights: The group chased B.M. on foot.
One member of the group had a knife which he held to B.M.’s throat.
The group kicked and punched the complainant.
B.M. was unconscious and having seizures when police arrived on the scene.
B.M. sustained serious injuries to his facial area, including a broken nose, bruises, and a swollen lip. He also sustained permanent brain injury.
the complainant came as close to dying from the assault as is possible without actually dying
rationale_highlights: The pre-sentence reports revealed that both have suffered tragic childhoods.
The sentencing judge was fully alive to both of these considerations.
The sentencing judge gave full consideration to the appellant’s Aboriginal status and tragic upbringing.
note: Court says factors were considered but never states they reduced culpability or sentence.

crime_highlights: the appellant was driving a stolen Silverado in an erratic manner in a mall parking lot
he went through a red light and collided with another vehicle
The appellant ordered him to get out of the car, tried to reach in to unlock the door
grabbed the driver by the shirt to try to get him out of the driver’s seat
The occupant of that vehicle tried to roll up the window.
rationale_highlights: All four of his grandparents and two of his great-grandparents attended residential schools.

the sentencing judge erred by failing to give tangible weight to the systemic and background factors present here which played a substantial part in bringing the appellant to court and which attenuate his moral blameworthiness
note: Para 15 and 20 also discuss reduced blameworthiness but passage length limited.
